Hi Jillian —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Run LLM-powered support assistant (generation + tool calling) for internal agents and public web chat
- Semantic search/embeddings for article retrieval + a re-ranker in front of the generator
- Predictable tail latency for agent flows (SLO: p95 < 400ms for short prompts)
- Expected steady traffic: ~50 req/s; peak bursts up to ~500 req/s lasting 2–3 minutes
- Data controls: VPC + customer-managed KMS for keys (private deployment preferred but evaluating Dedicated first)

Open items / asks from Acme to size Dedicated:
1) A small sample of 24–48 hours of request metadata (qps over time, avg payload token counts, embedding requests per minute).
2) Clarify percent of requests that use long-context generation (>2k tokens) vs short chat.
3) Any hard constraints on burst duration or sustained peak windows.

What we can provide right away:
- Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (initial sizing worksheet)
- Attachment: integration-diagram.png (suggested network/auth flow)

High-level technical guidance (short):
- SDK & auth: Our SDK supports API key usage for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private, we support mTLS and customer KMS integration. API keys can be scoped to routes for least privilege.
- Routing: We recommend policy-based routing — latency-first for agent-facing routes, cost-first for async embedding jobs. Canary routes are trivial to configure.
- Structured output / tool calling: We support tool calling primitives and JSON schema validation; we can return structured payloads or function-call style responses to your orchestrator.
- Embeddings & reranker: Run embeddings as a separate route with batched calls (we can auto-batch). For reranking, we typically run a light transformer on top of embeddings; we can colocate reranker inference on Dedicated if latency needs require it.
- Autoscaling & queues (Dedicated): Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools plus autoscale headroom. For your burst profile, we'll size a baseline to handle steady QPS and use autoscale + short-term burst capacity (queue + priority routing) to absorb spikes.

Proposed next steps:
- Please send the 48h traffic sample (acme-traffic-sample.csv).
- Book a technical deep-dive with our infra engineer (30–45m) — propose Tue/Wed next week.
- We'll produce a preliminary Dedicated sizing + cost estimate after reviewing the sample.

Thanks — copying Marissa to coordinate commercial next steps.

Thanks Jillian — that sample is exactly what we need. Answers inline and some concrete recommendations below.

Q1) Queueing / burst behavior:
- Dedicated exposes a managed request queue per customer pool. Short bursts are absorbed by the built-in queue (configurable max queue length and TTL). We also support priority lanes (e.g., agent UI routes > batch embedding routes).
- Backpressure: if the queue is full, we return a 429 with a Retry-After header. Clients can use exponential backoff or prefer prioritized routes for critical traffic.

Q2) Max recommended concurrency per GPU:
- Generation (short prompts): recommended 6–12 concurrent requests per A100-equivalent GPU depending on model size and max tokens. For your avg 40-token flows, we estimate ~10 concurrency/GPU.
- Long-context generation (3k tokens): concurrency drops to ~1–2 per GPU depending on KV cache memory; these are expensive and we recommend routing them to dedicated long-context nodes or limiting concurrency.
- Embeddings: embeddings are highly batch-friendly — throughput often measured in thousands of vectors/sec on a single GPU with batching. We recommend a separate embeddings pool with high batch window and smaller concurrency per-worker.

Q3) mTLS availability:
- mTLS is available for Private deployments immediately. For Dedicated (our hosted reserved capacity) we offer IP-restricted API keys and will enable mTLS on a per-customer basis (requires private peering + provisioning). We can run that during onboarding — recommend a short security call with your network team.

Sizing suggestion (initial):
- Baseline pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs to comfortably handle steady 50 req/s for short prompts + some embedding throughput.
- Autoscale policy: add 2 GPUs at 60% avg utilization, add further 2 GPUs at sustained queue length > 100 over 30s. This should allow spikes to 500 req/s with queue absorption for the 2–3 minute bursts you described.
- Concurrency settings: set generation concurrency ~10/GPU for short prompts; for long-context set a separate pool with concurrency 1–2 and route high-token jobs there.
- Cost optimization: enable prefix/KV caching for agent sessions and use reduced-precision quantization for reranker nodes where acceptable.

Operational next steps:

- Proposed tech deep-dive: Tue 2027-02-28 10:00am PT — I’ll invite our Infra lead (Michael Grant) and a Security engineer for the mTLS discussion.
- Please share a list of IPs/subnets for peering if you want mTLS enabled on Dedicated.
